# ai-toolkit-layer — the candy's internals

How the `ai-toolkit` candy is built. Read `/charly-image:layer` first for the general candy
authoring rules; this file records only what is specific to this candy.

MUST be invoked when editing the ai-toolkit candy, its pixi env, or the build/probe steps.

## Why the pin is a COMMIT, not a tag

`git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/ostris/ai-toolkit.git` returns **no tags at all**.
The only pinnable ref upstream offers is a commit, so `AI_TOOLKIT_REF` is a full sha and the
build asserts `git rev-parse HEAD` equals it — a typo'd sha would otherwise leave the clone on
the default branch and the image would ship whatever main happened to be that day.

## Why there is a pixi.toml AND a venv

They own different things, and neither is redundant:

- **`pixi.toml` owns the Python MINOR VERSION** (`==3.12.*`). ai-toolkit requires >=3.10 and
  recommends 3.12; the Arch host python is newer than the wheels torch publishes.
- **The venv owns ai-toolkit's dependency set**, built from the pinned commit's own
  `requirements.txt`. That file pins a **git revision of diffusers** (`git+https://github.com/
  huggingface/diffusers.git@c943837…`) alongside `torchao`, `transformers`, `peft` and
  `lycoris-lora` versions that upstream solves together and re-solves on its own cadence.
  Re-expressing that set in `[pypi-dependencies]` would fork upstream's solved set and drift.

This follows the org precedent set by `pod-unsloth-studio`, which bootstraps the Unsloth Studio
runtime venv at image-build time for the same reason: the upstream app owns its environment.

## Why the venv is at `<root>/venv` specifically

The UI worker resolves its interpreter itself — `ui/cron/pythonPath.ts` looks for
`<TOOLKIT_ROOT>/venv/bin/python` and then `<TOOLKIT_ROOT>/.venv/bin/python`, falling back to
`python3` on PATH. Building the venv at `/opt/ai-toolkit/venv` means the GUI-launched jobs get
the pinned venv **without** any PATH surgery.

## Application in the image, state in the volume

ai-toolkit has **no `--base-directory` flag** (ComfyUI does), and it writes `config/`,
`output/` and `datasets/` relative to its own root. So the volume is spliced in by **symlink**,
created in the start scripts at RUNTIME because the volume only exists once the container
starts:

```
/opt/ai-toolkit/{config,output,datasets}  ->  $HOME/ai-toolkit/{config,output,datasets}
```

The app tree is `chown`ed to the image user so the UI can write its own runtime state, and
upstream's `config/` examples are copied to `/opt/ai-toolkit/config.examples` at build time
before the symlink replaces the live `config/` — otherwise the examples would vanish on first
boot and every volume wipe.

## Two services, not one wrapper

The UI server (`dist/cron/fileServer.js`) and its job worker (`dist/cron/worker.js`) are
declared as separate `service:` entries with different priorities. Upstream starts both through
`concurrently`; supervising the wrapper would leave the two real PIDs as untracked
grandchildren, so a dead worker would look "running".

## The Z-Image canary check

`ai-toolkit-diffusers-zimage` imports `ZImagePipeline` from the venv. That single probe is the
contract every Z-Image job depends on, and it is a property of the **diffusers revision
ai-toolkit pins** — not of anything this candy installs. If upstream moves the git pin to a
revision without Z-Image support, the build fails here instead of at the first training job.

## Node.js

The UI is Next.js + a worker + a file server; it is **built at image time** (`npm ci && npm run
build`) so the supervised launch is immediate and never depends on network access at start. The
`layer-nodejs` candy supplies Node >= 20.
